text:
Sam Liu: quick q — for /v1/generate (streaming) where do we draw the line between preflight 4xx vs midstream 4xx vs 5xx? wondering about client behavior expectations.
Priya Patel: good one. my instinct: validation that can be determined before any tokens are emitted -> 4xx preflight. anything discovered after model started producing (e.g., prompt too long, tokenization overflow, invalid tool call discovered midstream) -> 4xx with field-level details. infra/resource/transient timeouts -> 5xx.
Jordan Kim: +1. we should also consider compatibility: older clients might treat any 4xx as fatal (no retry) and 5xx as retryable. if we start returning 422 midstream for transient things, customers will break.
Chris O'Neill: can we signal retryability explicitly in the envelope? propose adding a small top-level flag: "retryable": true|false and keep http semantics for human/readability. e.g. 422 + "retryable": true for backoff-aware clients.
Sam Liu: hmm i like that. example error shape?
Priya Patel: example we discussed in api review:```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "validation_error",
    "code": "prompt_too_long",
    "message": "Prompt tokens (4098) exceed model limit (4096)",
    "retryable": false,
    "details": {"field": "input.prompt", "max_tokens": "4096"}
  }
}
```
Jordan Kim: for midstream we might use `stream_interruption` type and include `partial_output` marker so consumers can decide to fallback. e.g.:```json
{
  "error": {"type":"stream_interruption","code":"kv_cache_full","message":"KV cache exhausted on host","retryable":true},
  "partial_output": "<base64-or-plain-truncated-output>"
}
```
Chris O'Neill: ops question: do we need to map these to specific http codes? like 400 vs 422 vs 503. customers ask for simple rules. my recommendation: validation preflight -> 400/422, midstream client-input issues -> 422, transient infra -> 503/502, capacity throttles -> 429. keep 4xx non-retryable by default unless `retryable:true` is present.
Sam Liu: agree on mapping. one policy we should call out in the contract doc: streaming endpoints must never silently drop errors — always emit a final error envelope event or close with a distinct code so clients can detect.
Priya Patel: +1. add a note about SDKs: our SDKs should surface `retryable` on exceptions and map 429/5xx auto-retries. non-SDK callers should read `error.retryable`.
Jordan Kim: edgecase: if user sends invalid JSON in a tool call inside the prompt, it's discovered midstream — do we treat as validation error (422 non-retryable) or allow a small client-side repair? i'd say 422 non-retryable.
Sam Liu: sounds good. action items: Priya to draft contract PR with precise shapes + migration notes; Jordan to add SDK handling examples; Chris to add server routing fallback guidance (how we decide to change 4xx -> fallback model). @deploy-bot please set an api-spec review on calendar for Friday. :calendar:
deploy-bot: created review event: "API error-shapes & streaming semantics" on Friday 10:00am, invited: Sam Liu, Priya Patel, Jordan Kim, Chris O'Neill.
Priya Patel: will start the PR and ping when ready for review. thanks! :thumbsup:
